drivingQuestion: Whose view is the mishna's ruling that levirate betrothal after ḥalitza is ineffective?
outcomeNote: Attribution statement; challenged in the next sugya

segments.he: חָלַץ וְעָשָׂה מַאֲמָר. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּאָמַר: אֵין קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בְּחַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין. אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יֵשׁ אַחַר חֲלִיצָה כְּלוּם.
segments.en: § It was taught in the mishna: If the yavam «performed ḥalitza and» then «performed levirate betrothal,» nothing is effective after ḥalitza and this levirate betrothal is not valid. «Rav Yehuda said» that «Rav said: This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva, who says» that «betrothal does not take effect on» those who are forbidden as they are «liable for» violating «a prohibition.» Once he has performed ḥalitza, the woman is forbidden to him due to the prohibition derived from the verse “So shall it be done to the man who does not build his brother’s house” (Deuteronomy 25:9), and betrothal is ineffective. «But the Rabbis say something is» effective «after ḥalitza.» Although the woman who performed ḥalitza is forbidden to him, if he does betroth her, his betrothal is effective, as with any regular prohibition.
